## Investigation

What communication and persistent state accompany one known, reversible
configuration change made by the official tool?

::: {.manual-prereq title="Require a recoverable, observed baseline"}

Proceed only if the previous records exist, the selected control is understood,
and the change is reversible without firmware flashing. Choose one variable—for
example pitch-bend range—and one before/after value. If recovery is uncertain,
stop at Stage 6. The active specification must name this exact control, both
values, the capture method, and the stop condition before any change is made.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Prepare metadata before touching the control"}

Copy the metadata template and create a local raw-capture directory:

```bash
cp evidence/templates/setting-capture.yml evidence/records/seaboard-block-01-setting-capture.yml
mkdir -p evidence/captures/seaboard-block-01
```

Record device, firmware if known, application version, transport, capture tool,
the exact control, and before value. Start with passive capture where possible.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Change one variable, then reverse it"}

Capture traffic before, during, and after one change. Repeat the same change,
then reverse it. Check the resulting device behaviour and power-cycle
persistence. Keep raw capture local until you have reviewed its contents and
redistribution status.

:::

::: {.manual-check title="Evaluate the protocol hypothesis"}

Call a message pattern a *hypothesis* only when repeated captures align with one
control change and its reversal. Record direction, payload candidates, device,
firmware, persistence, and confidence. Do not send a suspected message back to
the device in this stage.

:::
